blocks.source: Canto V
blocks.translation: Canto V

blocks.source: Così discesi del cerchio primaio
blocks.translation: Thus I descended out of the first circle

blocks.source: giù nel secondo, che men loco cinghia
blocks.translation: Down to the second, that less space begirds,

blocks.source: e tanto più dolor, che punge a guaio.
blocks.translation: And so much greater dole, that goads to wailing.

blocks.source: Stavvi Minòs orribilmente, e ringhia:
blocks.translation: There standeth Minos horribly, and snarls;

blocks.source: essamina le colpe ne l’intrata;
blocks.translation: Examines the transgressions at the entrance;

blocks.source: giudica e manda secondo ch’avvinghia.
blocks.translation: Judges, and sends according as he girds him.

blocks.source: Dico che quando l’anima mal nata
blocks.translation: I say, that when the spirit evil-born

blocks.source: li vien dinanzi, tutta si confessa;
blocks.translation: Cometh before him, wholly it confesses;

blocks.source: e quel conoscitor de le peccata
blocks.translation: And this discriminator of transgressions

blocks.source: vede qual loco d’inferno è da essa;
blocks.translation: Seeth what place in Hell is meet for it;

blocks.source: cignesi con la coda tante volte
blocks.translation: Girds himself with his tail as many times

blocks.source: quantunque gradi vuol che giù sia messa.
blocks.translation: As grades he wishes it should be thrust down.

blocks.source: Sempre dinanzi a lui ne stanno molte:
blocks.translation: Always before him many of them stand;

blocks.source: vanno a vicenda ciascuna al giudizio,
blocks.translation: They go by turns each one unto the judgment;

blocks.source: dicono e odono e poi son giù volte.
blocks.translation: They speak, and hear, and then are downward hurled.

blocks.source: «O tu che vieni al doloroso ospizio»,
blocks.translation: “O thou, that to this dolorous hostelry

blocks.source: disse Minòs a me quando mi vide,
blocks.translation: Comest,” said Minos to me, when he saw me,

blocks.source: lasciando l’atto di cotanto offizio,
blocks.translation: Leaving the practice of so great an office,

blocks.source: «guarda com’ entri e di cui tu ti fide;
blocks.translation: “Look how thou enterest, and in whom thou trustest;

blocks.source: non t’inganni l’ampiezza de l’intrare!».
blocks.translation: Let not the portal’s amplitude deceive thee.”

blocks.source: E ’l duca mio a lui: «Perché pur gride?
blocks.translation: And unto him my Guide: “Why criest thou too?

blocks.source: Non impedir lo suo fatale andare:
blocks.translation: Do not impede his journey fate-ordained;

blocks.source: vuolsi così colà dove si puote
blocks.translation: It is so willed there where is power to do

blocks.source: ciò che si vuole, e più non dimandare».
blocks.translation: That which is willed; and ask no further question.”

blocks.source: Or incomincian le dolenti note
blocks.translation: And now begin the dolesome notes to grow

blocks.source: a farmisi sentire; or son venuto
blocks.translation: Audible unto me; now am I come

blocks.source: là dove molto pianto mi percuote.
blocks.translation: There where much lamentation strikes upon me.

blocks.source: Io venni in loco d’ogne luce muto,
blocks.translation: I came into a place mute of all light,

blocks.source: che mugghia come fa mar per tempesta,
blocks.translation: Which bellows as the sea does in a tempest,

blocks.source: se da contrari venti è combattuto.
blocks.translation: If by opposing winds ’t is combated.

blocks.source: La bufera infernal, che mai non resta,
blocks.translation: The infernal hurricane that never rests

blocks.source: mena li spirti con la sua rapina;
blocks.translation: Hurtles the spirits onward in its rapine;

blocks.source: voltando e percotendo li molesta.
blocks.translation: Whirling them round, and smiting, it molests them.

blocks.source: Quando giungon davanti a la ruina,
blocks.translation: When they arrive before the precipice,

blocks.source: quivi le strida, il compianto, il lamento;
blocks.translation: There are the shrieks, the plaints, and the laments,

blocks.source: bestemmian quivi la virtù divina.
blocks.translation: There they blaspheme the puissance divine.

blocks.source: Intesi ch’a così fatto tormento
blocks.translation: I understood that unto such a torment

blocks.source: enno dannati i peccator carnali,
blocks.translation: The carnal malefactors were condemned,

blocks.source: che la ragion sommettono al talento.
blocks.translation: Who reason subjugate to appetite.

blocks.source: E come li stornei ne portan l’ali
blocks.translation: And as the wings of starlings bear them on

blocks.source: nel freddo tempo, a schiera larga e piena,
blocks.translation: In the cold season in large band and full,

blocks.source: così quel fiato li spiriti mali
blocks.translation: So doth that blast the spirits maledict;

blocks.source: di qua, di là, di giù, di sù li mena;
blocks.translation: It hither, thither, downward, upward, drives them;

blocks.source: nulla speranza li conforta mai,
blocks.translation: No hope doth comfort them for evermore,

blocks.source: non che di posa, ma di minor pena.
blocks.translation: Not of repose, but even of lesser pain.

blocks.source: E come i gru van cantando lor lai,
blocks.translation: And as the cranes go chanting forth their lays,

blocks.source: faccendo in aere di sé lunga riga,
blocks.translation: Making in air a long line of themselves,

blocks.source: così vid’ io venir, traendo guai,
blocks.translation: So saw I coming, uttering lamentations,

blocks.source: ombre portate da la detta briga;
blocks.translation: Shadows borne onward by the aforesaid stress.

blocks.source: per ch’i’ dissi: «Maestro, chi son quelle
blocks.translation: Whereupon said I: “Master, who are those

blocks.source: genti che l’aura nera sì gastiga?».
blocks.translation: People, whom the black air so castigates?”

blocks.source: «La prima di color di cui novelle
blocks.translation: “The first of those, of whom intelligence

blocks.source: tu vuo’ saper», mi disse quelli allotta,
blocks.translation: Thou fain wouldst have,” then said he unto me,

blocks.source: «fu imperadrice di molte favelle.
blocks.translation: “The empress was of many languages.

blocks.source: A vizio di lussuria fu sì rotta,
blocks.translation: To sensual vices she was so abandoned,

blocks.source: che libito fé licito in sua legge,
blocks.translation: That lustful she made licit in her law,

blocks.source: per tòrre il biasmo in che era condotta.
blocks.translation: To remove the blame to which she had been led.

blocks.source: Ell’ è Semiramìs, di cui si legge
blocks.translation: She is Semiramis, of whom we read

blocks.source: che succedette a Nino e fu sua sposa:
blocks.translation: That she succeeded Ninus, and was his spouse;

blocks.source: tenne la terra che ’l Soldan corregge.
blocks.translation: She held the land which now the Sultan rules.

blocks.source: L’altra è colei che s’ancise amorosa,
blocks.translation: The next is she who killed herself for love,

blocks.source: e ruppe fede al cener di Sicheo;
blocks.translation: And broke faith with the ashes of Sichaeus;

blocks.source: poi è Cleopatràs lussurïosa.
blocks.translation: Then Cleopatra the voluptuous.”

blocks.source: Elena vedi, per cui tanto reo
blocks.translation: Helen I saw, for whom so many ruthless

blocks.source: tempo si volse, e vedi ’l grande Achille,
blocks.translation: Seasons revolved; and saw the great Achilles,

blocks.source: che con amore al fine combatteo.
blocks.translation: Who at the last hour combated with Love.

blocks.source: Vedi Parìs, Tristano»; e più di mille
blocks.translation: Paris I saw, Tristan; and more than a thousand

blocks.source: ombre mostrommi e nominommi a dito,
blocks.translation: Shades did he name and point out with his finger,

blocks.source: ch’amor di nostra vita dipartille.
blocks.translation: Whom Love had separated from our life.

blocks.source: Poscia ch’io ebbi ’l mio dottore udito
blocks.translation: After that I had listened to my Teacher,

blocks.source: nomar le donne antiche e ’ cavalieri,
blocks.translation: Naming the dames of eld and cavaliers,

blocks.source: pietà mi giunse, e fui quasi smarrito.
blocks.translation: Pity prevailed, and I was nigh bewildered.

blocks.source: I’ cominciai: «Poeta, volontieri
blocks.translation: And I began: “O Poet, willingly

blocks.source: parlerei a quei due che ’nsieme vanno,
blocks.translation: Speak would I to those two, who go together,

blocks.source: e paion sì al vento esser leggeri».
blocks.translation: And seem upon the wind to be so light.”

blocks.source: Ed elli a me: «Vedrai quando saranno
blocks.translation: And, he to me: “Thou’lt mark, when they shall be

blocks.source: più presso a noi; e tu allor li priega
blocks.translation: Nearer to us; and then do thou implore them

blocks.source: per quello amor che i mena, ed ei verranno».
blocks.translation: By love which leadeth them, and they will come.”

blocks.source: Sì tosto come il vento a noi li piega,
blocks.translation: Soon as the wind in our direction sways them,

blocks.source: mossi la voce: «O anime affannate,
blocks.translation: My voice uplift I: “O ye weary souls!

blocks.source: venite a noi parlar, s’altri nol niega!».
blocks.translation: Come speak to us, if no one interdicts it.”

blocks.source: Quali colombe dal disio chiamate
blocks.translation: As turtle-doves, called onward by desire,

blocks.source: con l’ali alzate e ferme al dolce nido
blocks.translation: With open and steady wings to the sweet nest

blocks.source: vegnon per l’aere, dal voler portate;
blocks.translation: Fly through the air by their volition borne,

blocks.source: cotali uscir de la schiera ov’ è Dido,
blocks.translation: So came they from the band where Dido is,

blocks.source: a noi venendo per l’aere maligno,
blocks.translation: Approaching us athwart the air malign,

blocks.source: sì forte fu l’affettüoso grido.
blocks.translation: So strong was the affectionate appeal.

blocks.source: «O animal grazïoso e benigno
blocks.translation: “O living creature gracious and benignant,

blocks.source: che visitando vai per l’aere perso
blocks.translation: Who visiting goest through the purple air

blocks.source: noi che tignemmo il mondo di sanguigno,
blocks.translation: Us, who have stained the world incarnadine,

blocks.source: se fosse amico il re de l’universo,
blocks.translation: If were the King of the Universe our friend,

blocks.source: noi pregheremmo lui de la tua pace,
blocks.translation: We would pray unto him to give thee peace,

blocks.source: poi c’hai pietà del nostro mal perverso.
blocks.translation: Since thou hast pity on our woe perverse.

blocks.source: Di quel che udire e che parlar vi piace,
blocks.translation: Of what it pleases thee to hear and speak,

blocks.source: noi udiremo e parleremo a voi,
blocks.translation: That will we hear, and we will speak to you,

blocks.source: mentre che ’l vento, come fa, ci tace.
blocks.translation: While silent is the wind, as it is now.

blocks.source: Siede la terra dove nata fui
blocks.translation: Sitteth the city, wherein I was born,

blocks.source: su la marina dove ’l Po discende
blocks.translation: Upon the sea-shore where the Po descends

blocks.source: per aver pace co’ seguaci sui.
blocks.translation: To rest in peace with all his retinue.

blocks.source: Amor, ch’al cor gentil ratto s’apprende,
blocks.translation: Love, that on gentle heart doth swiftly seize,

blocks.source: prese costui de la bella persona
blocks.translation: Seized this man for the person beautiful

blocks.source: che mi fu tolta; e ’l modo ancor m’offende.
blocks.translation: That was ta’en from me, and still the mode offends me.

blocks.source: Amor, ch’a nullo amato amar perdona,
blocks.translation: Love, that exempts no one beloved from loving,

blocks.source: mi prese del costui piacer sì forte,
blocks.translation: Seized me with pleasure of this man so strongly,

blocks.source: che, come vedi, ancor non m’abbandona.
blocks.translation: That, as thou seest, it doth not yet desert me;

blocks.source: Amor condusse noi ad una morte.
blocks.translation: Love has conducted us unto one death;

blocks.source: Caina attende chi a vita ci spense».
blocks.translation: Caina waiteth him who quenched our life!”

blocks.source: Queste parole da lor ci fuor porte.
blocks.translation: These words were borne along from them to us.

blocks.source: Quand’ io intesi quell’ anime offense,
blocks.translation: As soon as I had heard those souls tormented,

blocks.source: china’ il viso, e tanto il tenni basso,
blocks.translation: I bowed my face, and so long held it down

blocks.source: fin che ’l poeta mi disse: «Che pense?».
blocks.translation: Until the Poet said to me: “What thinkest?”

blocks.source: Quando rispuosi, cominciai: «Oh lasso,
blocks.translation: When I made answer, I began: “Alas!

blocks.source: quanti dolci pensier, quanto disio
blocks.translation: How many pleasant thoughts, how much desire,

blocks.source: menò costoro al doloroso passo!».
blocks.translation: Conducted these unto the dolorous pass!”

blocks.source: Poi mi rivolsi a loro e parla’ io,
blocks.translation: Then unto them I turned me, and I spake,

blocks.source: e cominciai: «Francesca, i tuoi martìri
blocks.translation: And I began: “Thine agonies, Francesca,

blocks.source: a lagrimar mi fanno tristo e pio.
blocks.translation: Sad and compassionate to weeping make me.

blocks.source: Ma dimmi: al tempo d’i dolci sospiri,
blocks.translation: But tell me, at the time of those sweet sighs,

blocks.source: a che e come concedette amore
blocks.translation: By what and in what manner Love conceded,

blocks.source: che conosceste i dubbiosi disiri?».
blocks.translation: That you should know your dubious desires?”

blocks.source: E quella a me: «Nessun maggior dolore
blocks.translation: And she to me: “There is no greater sorrow

blocks.source: che ricordarsi del tempo felice
blocks.translation: Than to be mindful of the happy time

blocks.source: ne la miseria; e ciò sa ’l tuo dottore.
blocks.translation: In misery, and that thy Teacher knows.

blocks.source: Ma s’a conoscer la prima radice
blocks.translation: But, if to recognise the earliest root

blocks.source: del nostro amor tu hai cotanto affetto,
blocks.translation: Of love in us thou hast so great desire,

blocks.source: dirò come colui che piange e dice.
blocks.translation: I will do even as he who weeps and speaks.

blocks.source: Noi leggiavamo un giorno per diletto
blocks.translation: One day we reading were for our delight

blocks.source: di Lancialotto come amor lo strinse;
blocks.translation: Of Launcelot, how Love did him enthral.

blocks.source: soli eravamo e sanza alcun sospetto.
blocks.translation: Alone we were and without any fear.

blocks.source: Per più fïate li occhi ci sospinse
blocks.translation: Full many a time our eyes together drew

blocks.source: quella lettura, e scolorocci il viso;
blocks.translation: That reading, and drove the colour from our faces;

blocks.source: ma solo un punto fu quel che ci vinse.
blocks.translation: But one point only was it that o’ercame us.

blocks.source: Quando leggemmo il disïato riso
blocks.translation: When as we read of the much-longed-for smile

blocks.source: esser basciato da cotanto amante,
blocks.translation: Being by such a noble lover kissed,

blocks.source: questi, che mai da me non fia diviso,
blocks.translation: This one, who ne’er from me shall be divided,

blocks.source: la bocca mi basciò tutto tremante.
blocks.translation: Kissed me upon the mouth all palpitating.

blocks.source: Galeotto fu ’l libro e chi lo scrisse:
blocks.translation: Galeotto was the book and he who wrote it.

blocks.source: quel giorno più non vi leggemmo avante».
blocks.translation: That day no farther did we read therein.”

blocks.source: Mentre che l’uno spirto questo disse,
blocks.translation: And all the while one spirit uttered this,

blocks.source: l’altro piangëa; sì che di pietade
blocks.translation: The other one did weep so, that, for pity,

blocks.source: io venni men così com’ io morisse.
blocks.translation: I swooned away as if I had been dying,

blocks.source: E caddi come corpo morto cade.
blocks.translation: And fell, even as a dead body falls.
